correctness.rationale: The diagonal-coordinate Jacobian, variance normalization, integrability thresholds, and endpoint scalings were reconstructed explicitly. In the regular regime the tube area gives \(2\sqrt3\,\pi y\) times \(\int f^3\). At a critical endpoint the \(t^{-1}\) diagonal density produces exactly one half-log from a lower cutoff of order \(\sqrt y\), yielding \(\sqrt3\,\pi B^{-3}\) per critical endpoint. In the subcritical regime the exact scaling \(X_i=\sqrt y\,u_i\) produces \(y^{3m/2}\); simplex radial integration shows \(J_m\) is finite exactly for \(m<2/3\). The critical \(\operatorname{Beta}(2/3,1)\) coefficient exactly matches Royen after \(Q=2S^2\). Finite code checks verify only normalization identities, not the infinite-limit theorem.

The 2026 motivating paper treats the three-observation distribution and gives a singular arcsine endpoint law but does not state the full two-parameter lower-tail Beta phase diagram. The surviving claim is the exact \(n=3\) two-endpoint localization with all three leading constants and the endpoint competition/addition rule. Searches found no published finding or inspected primary statement implying that full claim.

value.rationale: The recent source makes singular bounded parents and the small-variance endpoint behavior a live exact-distribution problem. The theorem identifies precisely when the usual linear tube law fails, locates the logarithmic transition, and supplies exact constants that separate one-endpoint from tied two-endpoint singularity. This is useful for stable tail evaluation and for understanding why the arcsine case has exponent \(3/4\). The result is not merely a recomputation of Royen: it makes the full two-parameter Beta endpoint competition explicit while carefully excluding already-covered pure-power content.
